tagger.biberplus.about: Tagger for Biber's (1988) features for multidimensional analysis, with extensions for web texts.
tagger.biberplus.name: BiberPlus
tagger.biberplus.opt.binary_tags.explain: Includes BiberPlus binary features (presence or absence) in addition to counts.
tagger.biberplus.opt.binary_tags.name: Binary tags
tagger.biberplus.opt.function_words.expl: Also counts each function word as its own feature. Greatly increases the number of columns.
tagger.biberplus.opt.function_words.name: Function words
tagger.biberplus.opt.n_processes.name: Processes
tagger.biberplus.opt.processing_size.exp: How many characters BiberPlus processes per chunk.
tagger.mfte.about: Multi-Feature Tagger of English (Le Foll): features for multidimensional analysis, on top of Stanza classes.
tagger.mfte.name: MFTE
tagger.mfte.opt.components.explain: mfte = MFTE features; pos and morph come from the underlying Stanza analysis.
tagger.mfte.opt.components.name: What to extract
tagger.mfte.opt.device.explain: auto uses an NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) if present; otherwise the CPU.
tagger.mfte.opt.device.name: Device
tagger.mfte.opt.extended.explain: Adds the semantic and stance classes (stance verbs, nouns, adjectives and clauses). Changes the feature set.
tagger.mfte.opt.extended.name: Extended mode
tagger.mfte.opt.lang.name: Language
tagger.mfte.opt.model_dir.explain: Where the Stanza models used by MFTE are stored.
tagger.mfte.opt.model_dir.name: Stanza model folder
tagger.reason.torch_numpy: torch in this package cannot use numpy ({error}). On Intel macOS numpy<2 is required
tagger.spacy.about: Fast statistical tagger. Gives universal class (UPOS), Penn Treebank tag, lemma and morphology.
tagger.spacy.name: spaCy
tagger.spacy.opt.batch_size.explain: How many texts spaCy processes at once. Larger values use more memory.
tagger.spacy.opt.batch_size.name: Batch size
tagger.spacy.opt.components.explain: pos = universal class (UPOS); tag = Penn Treebank tag; lemma = dictionary form; morph = morphological features (number, tense...). Dropping lemma is slightly faster.
tagger.spacy.opt.components.name: What to extract
tagger.spacy.opt.max_length.explain: Character limit per text (max_length). Avoids errors on very long texts; longer texts use more memory.
tagger.spacy.opt.max_length.name: Maximum text length
tagger.spacy.opt.model.explain: spaCy statistical model. Larger ones (md, lg) and the transformer-based one (trf) are usually more accurate, slower and heavier.
tagger.spacy.opt.model.name: Model
tagger.spacy.opt.n_process.explain: Parallel processes (spaCy n_process). Helps with large corpora; each process loads the model.
tagger.spacy.opt.n_process.name: Processes
tagger.stanza.about: Stanford neural tagger (uses torch). Slower than spaCy, with models per treebank. Gives UPOS, XPOS, features and, if asked, lemma.
tagger.stanza.name: Stanza
tagger.stanza.opt.components.explain: pos = UPOS and XPOS; morph = morphological features (come with pos); lemma = dictionary form (loads another model and is slower).
tagger.stanza.opt.components.name: What to extract
tagger.stanza.opt.device.explain: auto uses an NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) if present; otherwise the CPU. Apple GPU (MPS) is excluded because it is slower here.
tagger.stanza.opt.device.name: Device
tagger.stanza.opt.lang.explain: Corpus language; selects the models to load.
tagger.stanza.opt.lang.name: Language
tagger.stanza.opt.model_dir.explain: Where Stanza models are stored. Empty = Stanza default folder (or STANZA_RESOURCES_DIR).
tagger.stanza.opt.model_dir.name: Model folder
tagger.stanza.opt.package.explain: Model set. default = recommended combined models; default_fast = faster; default_accurate = transformer, more accurate and much slower; the others are trained on a single treebank (ewt, gum...) and may change XPOS tags.
tagger.stanza.opt.package.name: Package (treebank)
tagger.stanza.opt.pos_batch_size.explain: How many words the tagger processes per batch. Larger = faster, more memory.
tagger.stanza.opt.pos_batch_size.name: POS batch size
tagger.stanza.opt.tokenize_no_ssplit.exp: Treats each paragraph (separated by a blank line) as one sentence. Useful when the text is already segmented.
Assumes words are separated by spaces and sentences by newlines; Stanza does not tokenize again.
